alignments.note: Imperative rendered by the bare English verb.
Preposition governing the pronoun; rule 36 keeps *for* on the preposition rather than on the verb.
Causal conjunction rendered *for*; postpositive in Greek, clause-initial in English under rule 15.
Inflected passive verb takes its supplied subject and auxiliary under rule 9; head on the lexical participle *persuaded*, not on *are*.
Reported speech with an expressed complementizer, so rule 43's unrepresented case does not apply.
Verb with its supplied subject pronoun under rule 9; head on the lexical verb. Not a light-verb collapse under rule 73, since the ASV spells both *have* and *conscience* out.
Attributive adjective; bare *good*, the supplied determiner going to the noun under rule 58.

Both adjective and noun are anarthrous, so rule 58 gives the supplied *a* to the noun, discontinuously under rule 15. Reading *a* as a rule 7 helper on the adjective it stands next to is what rule 58 forbids.
Circumstantial participle rendered by an English participle.

No conjunction governs the clause, so the infinitival *to* is rule 7's ordinary helper on its own verb rather than rule 40's clause-introducer. The middle's reflexive sense is carried by the intransitive *live* itself, so no separate reflexive pronoun competes.
Preposition rendered *in*; the ASV writes it out separately, so no compound unit under rule 94.
Substantival adjective expanded with the generic noun *things*; rule 17 heads it on *all*. No article stands here, so rule 102's article-owns-the-nominal case does not arise.
